backing.backing_score_basis: MEASURES SUBORDINATION ADEQUACY — HOW MUCH JUNIOR CAPITAL SITS BELOW THE SENIOR BEFORE IT TAKES LOSS — NOT COLLATERAL QUALITY AND NOT A COLLATERAL RATIO. ⚠️ THE FEED COMPUTES NO BACKING FOR THIS ASSET (`collateral_ratio: null`, `total_backing: null`), so this authored number is the ONLY figure on the axis and nothing cross-checks it. ⚠️ CUT 5.5 -> 5.0 on 2026-09-06 ON THE SUBORDINATION SERIES: the senior's first-loss attachment point measured 9.66% on 2026-08-24 and is 7.94% today — 21% THINNER IN 13 DAYS, the fourth consecutive reading in the same direction. ✅ AND FOR THE FIRST TIME IT IS BASIS-INDEPENDENT: it falls on the conservative $20M waterfall basis (11.06% -> 7.94%) AND on the $73M balance-sheet basis (40.36% -> 28.98%), so the finding no longer depends on resolving Re's own contradiction between the two. ⚠️ THE MECHANISM IS DILUTION BY GROWTH, NOT DETERIORATION: the junior layer is measurably FLAT (+0.4% in three weeks, $72.97M by /tvl residual arithmetic) against senior growth of +39.3%. No claim event, combined ratio still 92%, no treaty above 99%. ⚠️ THE ATTACHMENT POINT THINNED BECAUSE THE DENOMINATOR ROSE — growth reading as health is exactly why it passed unnoticed for four readings. ⚠️ NOT LOWER THAN 5.0: collateral quality is unchanged and the loss threshold still requires a ~115% combined ratio against a realised 92%.

backing.backing_score_tranche: ⚠️ THIS IS THE SENIOR TRANCHE, AND THE ATTACHMENT POINT SCORED HERE COUNTS reUSDe AS PART OF ITS OWN CUSHION. Re's waterfall (docs.re.xyz, confirmed 2026-09-11): premiums -> Re capital (junior, 3.9% impairment) -> reUSDe (mezzanine, 0.9%) -> reUSD (senior, 0.03%). ⚠️ SO THE 2026-09-06 CUT ON THE ATTACHMENT SERIES IS A SENIOR-SPECIFIC MEASUREMENT AND MUST NOT BE PROPAGATED TO reUSDe — reUSDe's own cushion is Re capital alone, and importing this figure would use a denominator containing the tranche being scored. reusde-re holds backing 5.5 for that reason and the gap is correct, not stale.

liquidity.liquidity_score_basis: ⚠️ MEASURES THE WORSE OF TWO LEGS — VENUE DEPTH AND PRIMARY REDEMPTION — AND THE BINDING LEG IS REDEMPTION, NOT DEPTH. Venue leg scores 5.0; redemption scores 4.5; the axis takes the worse. ⚠️⚠️ SO THE COMPUTED DEPTH FIGURE BESIDE THIS SCORE IS NOT WHAT THIS SCORE MEASURES. The feed's `total_2pct_depth` of $10,000,000 (status `bracketed`, is_floor false) describes the VENUE LEG ALONE — the leg that is NOT binding. A reader comparing 4.5 against $10M is comparing our worse-leg score to their better-leg measurement and will read a disagreement that does not exist. ⚠️ REDEMPTION IS THE WORSE LEG FOR A SPECIFIC AND COHORT-DEPENDENT REASON: A U.S. PERSON HAS NO PRIMARY CHANNEL AT ALL. For non-U.S. holders primary redemption at NAV works and the venue question is largely moot; for U.S. holders the DEX route is the only route. Venue detail: DEX-only, no CEX fallback, Ethereum-concentrated, ~$946k/24h across four pools (Fluid 63%, Curve REUSD/SUSDE 37%, two pools <1%) — roughly $28M/month against a $176M market cap, functional at retail size and thin at institutional size. ⚠️ THE SCORE IS AN AVERAGE ACROSS COHORTS AND IS THEREFORE WRONG FOR BOTH: a non-U.S. institutional holder faces a better exit than 4.5 implies, a U.S. holder a worse one. ✅ CORRECTED 5.0 -> 4.5 on 2026-09-06 — the row had been scoring the venue leg alone while the Overall row's arithmetic already used 4.5, so this corrected the file to itself rather than re-scoring it; overall unchanged at 5.0. Caught by tidresearch mid-migration, who noticed frontmatter and the Overall enumeration disagreed.

Re's reinsurance book sits beneath an sUSDe collateral layer, which IMPORTS ETHENA RISK INTO A REINSURANCE PRODUCT — a dependency a buyer of reinsurance exposure is unlikely to expect. Measured composition is 99.98% Ethena-derived (sUSDe 99.05%). ⚠️ SO THE TWO RISKS ARE UNCORRELATED IN SOURCE AND FULLY CORRELATED IN THE VEHICLE: an Ethena event and an insurance-loss event are independent causes that land on the same holder through the same instrument.
